text:
alex: Quick follow-up from the RFC split — leaning toward an allocator/executor split + cohort routing for cost vs SLA tradeoffs. Allocator picks execution pool based on SLA tag, model family, and inferred latency budget.
priya: Sounds reasonable. Main question: where do RBAC checks live? fast-path in allocator or in the executor? :thinking_face:
alex: Prefer allocator for allow/deny so we fail fast and avoid expensive model runs. Executor stays stateless (just runs). Tradeoff: allocator needs a small auth cache + webhook invalidation.
mateo: Auth cache invalidation is the nasty bit — permission change -> stale allow. How do we avoid leaks?
ben: We can use short TTL (30s) + push invalidation via user-perm webhook. Also write a decision log for audit.
lina: Also thinking about prefix/KV cache locality — if allocator routes cohorts by quantization or model variant, cache hit rate could drop.
alex: Yep. We'll group cohorts to preserve cache locality: cohort keys = (model_family, quantization_profile, SLA_bucket). That keeps hot prefixes together.
priya: Rollout plan?
alex: Canary 10% traffic with cohort routing feature-flagged off by default per tenant. Observe for 48h. Metrics to watch: p50/p95 latency, token RPS, auth_hit_rate, cache_miss_rate, 5xx rate, and cost-per-token. If auth_hit_rate < 90% or 5xx spikes > +0.5% rollback.
mateo: Can we get a smoke test that toggles permission and verifies immediate deny after invalidation?
alex: Created ticket CONSOLE-1429 for the smoke + automated invalidation test. Quick script snippet:
```bash
# smoke: hit allocator then flip permission via test webhook
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer TEST' -X POST https://console.internal/api/v1/query -d '{"q":"SELECT 1"}'
# then call webhook to revoke
curl -X POST https://authhook.internal/invalidate -d '{"user":"test"}'
```
ops-bot: deploy: canary queued for infra-qa at 2026-03-20T22:00Z :rocket:
ben: I'll own the cache invalidation hooks and the decision log entries.
priya: I'll own RBAC test matrix + automation. :thumbsup:
alex: Thanks — follow-ups: CONSOLE-1429 (smoke), CONSOLE-1430 (auth-cache infra work), CONSOLE-1431 (metrics dashboard). We'll meet Thurs for a short sync.
